historical_claims.anchor: Jameson appears very early in the Spider-Man story, in the first issue of The Amazing Spider-Man in 1963.
In Amazing Spider-Man number twenty, Jameson's campaign helps create the Scorpion.
Mac Gargan, a private investigator, receives dangerous enhancements through scientist Farley Stillwell, with Jameson financing the scheme.
Spider-Man ends up protecting the very man who helped create the problem.
Professor Spencer Smythe builds a Spider-Slayer robot, and Jameson pays to use it against Spider-Man.
Robbie Robertson, in particular, provides an important counterweight to the editor's anger.

historical_claims.anchor: In Raimi's first Spider-Man, Jonah refuses to reveal Peter Parker as the source of photographs when threatened by the Green Goblin.
One of the most interesting late interventions comes in Chip Zdarsky and Michael Walsh's Peter Parker: The Spectacular Spider-Man number six, published in 2017.
By the end, Peter reveals his identity to Jonah.
